MessageExecutionStatus.description: Durable input execution status, independent of MessageStatus. Queued is established only by atomic executable submission and delivery commitment. Acknowledgement does not start execution. Started is terminal for this input status; cancelled and failed are confirmed pre-execution outcomes. Workflow-answer evidence and legacy messages without established admission evidence omit this field.

MessageExecutionAdmissionDisposition.description: The execution owner\'s recorded admission decision for an executable input, written once from its correlated acceptance. PENDING: the owner has not confirmed admission (offline, or delivery is ambiguous). IMMEDIATE: admitted and reserved to run next with nothing ahead of it. QUEUED: admitted to wait behind active work, earlier inputs, or an execution hold. Independent of executionStatus; IMMEDIATE does not mean started, and timeline placement still happens only at execution start. Present exactly when executionStatus is present.

FeatureSyncAnalyzePromptPayload.description: Payload for the feature-sync analyze EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=feature_sync_analyze). discrepancies.description: The outstanding discrepancies the previous turn surfaced. Rendered into the iterate prompt as the \"Outstanding items\" section so the agent reasons over them explicitly.

userMessage.description: The user\'s change request on the previously-surfaced discrepancy set. Termination is enforced by the submit_resolved / submit_revised submission tools.

FeatureSyncIteratePromptPayload.description: Payload for the feature-sync iterate EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=feature_sync_iterate). The wire payload carries the outstanding discrepancies the previous analyze (or iterate) turn surfaced — the iterate prompt renders them directly rather than relying on conversation history.

id.description: Stable identifier the platform assigns to a flagged item so user decisions and later revised sets can refer back to it.

summary.description: Short product-language statement of what looks off.

rationale.description: One- or two-sentence reason the item was flagged.

entityType.description: The kind of entity the discrepancy points at, when it points at a specific entity. Omitted when the gap is structural rather than entity-scoped.

entityId.description: Canonical id of the entity the discrepancy points at, paired with `entityType`.

proposal.description: Concrete remediation the agent proposes for this discrepancy, when it has one in mind.

FeatureSyncDiscrepancy.description: A single discrepancy surfaced by the feature-sync analyze turn when it detects drift between a declared feature/task and the observed code. Mirrors the server-side `featureSyncDiscrepancySchema` in api/src/flows/nodes/feature-sync/schemas.ts and is the canonical wire shape carried into the iterate trigger payload so the iterate prompt can render the outstanding items directly instead of leaning on conversation history.

projectId.description: Canonical id of the project whose feature tree the conversation is anchored on. Seeds the skeleton fetch the CLI performs at session init.

userMessage.description: Optional free-form text from the user (e.g. the initial ask that opened the conversation). Termination is conversational — controlled by the user, not by the payload.

FeatureTreeConversationPromptPayload.description: Payload for the feature-tree-conversation EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=feature_tree_conversation). The CLI fetches the project\'s feature tree skeleton at session init via `GET /projects/{projectId}/features/skeleton` and injects it into the agent\'s system prompt, so the wire payload only carries the project handle plus the optional user message that triggered the turn.

markdown.description: Complete visible plan. Preserve this exact text through approval and implementation.

discrepancies.description: Findings persisted with this plan version. Historical versions may omit the finding metadata.

suspectedImpact.description: A material inference that is not established by observation.

findingId.description: Stable identity that a finding keeps across replacement plan versions.

category.description: Kind of concern, independent of severity. project_context marks a conflict with recorded requirements, Contracts, designs or other governing context.

userDirection.description: The direction or assent the user gave about this finding.

disposition.description: Current state of the finding. Assent changes the disposition and never removes the finding. changes_existing_behavior marks a planned change to existing behavior that recorded design supports. repair_planned is the legacy name of changes_existing_behavior, accepted on read only so plans saved before the rename stay valid.

implementationFollowThrough.description: What implementation must address or verify for this finding.

withdrawalEvidence.description: Evidence that a withdrawn finding was mistaken or moot.

userMessage.description: Optional free-form hint from the user (e.g. \"focus on the auth stage\"). The agent produces unstructured narrative; termination is enforced by the submit_no_discrepancy / submit_discrepancies submission tools, not by the payload.

Mirrors `FeatureSyncAnalyzePromptPayload` but anchors the analyze turn on a plan and its design doc rather than a task: the plan-shaping flow walks the design-doc-declared structure instead of a task-seeded feature-tree, so the wire payload binds the plan id and design doc id explicitly rather than the task seed.

planId.description: Canonical delivering Plan identity from the persisted plan seed.

designDocId.description: Authoritative design document from the persisted plan seed.

discrepancies.description: The outstanding flagged items, each with its stable `id`, in the order the user saw them.

userMessage.description: The user\'s change request on the flagged items. Termination is enforced by the submit_revised submission tool.

PlanShapingFeatureSyncIteratePromptPaylo.description: Payload for the plan-shaping feature-sync iterate EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=plan_shaping_feature_sync_iterate). Every trigger carries the outstanding flagged items in display order and the user\'s per-item choices, so the turn never depends on provider session history to know what the user is referring to.

itemId.description: The `id` of the flagged item the choice applies to.

PlanShapingFeatureSyncItemDecision.description: The user\'s choice on one flagged feature-sync item. Guides the next revision pass only; it never approves a proposal or advances the review.

stageIdx.description: Zero-based index of the current stage within the plan\'s ordered durable stages. The first half of the 2-D `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor. The agent MUST echo this value back verbatim on its `submit_phase_breakdown` payload so the API can detect cursor divergence and synthesize an ERROR-class completion.

phaseIdx.description: Zero-based index of `journeyStep` within stage `stageIdx`\'s journey. The second half of the 2-D `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor. The agent MUST echo this value back verbatim on its `submit_phase_breakdown` payload so the API can detect cursor divergence and synthesize an ERROR-class completion.

phasesInStage.description: Number of journey steps in stage `stageIdx`\'s journey — the count of phases that share this stage. Derived API-side by grouping `FlowContext.journeySteps` by stage. Pairs with `phaseIdx` (which is per-stage) so the prompt can render an honest \"phase N of M in this stage\" header; `totalPhases` counts the whole map and would mismatch a per-stage `phaseIdx`.

totalPhases.description: Total number of journey steps in `FlowContext.journeySteps` across every stage. Used for whole-map accounting, not the per-stage position header (that pairs `phaseIdx` with `phasesInStage`).

designDocId.description: Canonical id of the plan\'s design document. Read via get_full_entity({ entities: [{ entityType: \'DESIGN_DOC\', entityId: designDocId }] }) to keep stage/step proposals consistent with the approved design.

planId.description: Canonical id of the plan being expanded. The agent creates stages and steps against this plan.

priorPhases.description: Steps-only output of every earlier phase in this journey, derived API-side from the entries in `FlowContext.accumulatedPhases` whose `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor precedes the trigger\'s. Sorted ascending by cursor. Absent or empty on the first phase. Each entry carries the actual steps the earlier phase emitted, so the current phase agent can stay consistent with what is already in the accumulating plan without re-reading prose summaries.

approvedVisuals.description: Every Mockup and Diagram the user approved as the visual set, in presentation order. Binding planning context: the steps must implement what these visuals show.

userMessage.description: Optional free-form text from the user. Carried for wire-shape symmetry; phase-breakdown does not accept user messages in v1.

PlanShapingPhaseBreakdownPromptPayload.description: Payload for the plan-shaping phase-breakdown EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=plan_shaping_phase_breakdown). Fires once per journey step after the user approves the JourneyMap. Phase identity is the 2-D `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor — `stageIdx` indexes the plan\'s durable stages, `phaseIdx` indexes the journey step within that stage\'s journey — derived API-side from the already-accumulated phases on FlowContext rather than from a separate counter. The agent investigates the journey step (reading the design doc, the parent feature hierarchy, and the relevant code) and emits a steps-only `{ stageIdx, phaseIdx, plan: { steps } }` payload via `submit_phase_breakdown`. The agent does NOT author PLAN_STEP proposals during the turn and never authors stages — the stage backbone is durable and pre-existing. The workflow accumulates each phase\'s payload on FlowContext and materializes every phase\'s steps in one transaction immediately before the FINALIZE transition fires.

id.description: Stable slug identifying this step within the JourneyMap (e.g. `step-1-open-conversation`). Used as a join key when the phase-breakdown agent reports against this step.

stageId.description: UUID of the durable PlanStage this journey step (phase) belongs under. Authored by proposed-stages before the journey-map turn runs; the phase-breakdown agent binds every `PhaseBreakdownStep` it emits for this phase to this same stage.

title.description: Short user-facing label naming what the user does or sees.

description.description: One- or two-sentence plain-language description of what the user does or sees in this step. Implementation detail belongs in `implementationNotes`, not here.

isUserInteractive.description: True when the user submits a form, clicks a button, or receives a direct UI response in this step. Used by ValidateIntegration as the anchor flag for validation checkpoints.

implementationNotes.description: Plain-language implementation bullets for this step, each annotated with the platform service that owns the work (or null for cross-cutting notes).

JourneyStep.description: One ordered step in a user-journey plan view — one *phase* of the journey. Describes what the user does or sees (not what the code does), plus the implementation work required and the services involved. `stageId` binds the step to the durable PlanStage whose journey it belongs to: the journey-map agent emits one journey per existing stage, so every step names its parent stage. `isUserInteractive` is the validation anchor flag — steps marked true are where ValidateIntegration checkpoints attach when validation is enabled. Authored by the journey-map agent and consumed downstream by each phase-breakdown agent turn.

text.description: Plain-language implementation bullet attached to the parent journey step.

serviceId.description: Canonical id of the platform service clearly responsible for the note, or null when the work is cross-cutting / no single service is clearly responsible.

serviceName.description: Human-readable name of the service identified by `serviceId`. Null when `serviceId` is null.

ServiceNote.description: One implementation-note bullet attached to a JourneyStep. Names a plain-language piece of implementation work and the platform service that owns it. `serviceId` and `serviceName` are nullable to express cross-cutting notes that no single service clearly owns; both fields must be present (nullable) so consumers do not have to distinguish \"missing\" from \"intentionally null\".

stageIdx.description: Zero-based stage index of the prior phase. With `phaseIdx`, the 2-D cursor that located the prior phase. Used only as a label here; the current phase\'s expected cursor is the top-level trigger field.

phaseIdx.description: Zero-based index of the prior phase\'s journey step within stage `stageIdx`\'s journey. Used only as a label here; the current phase\'s expected cursor is the top-level trigger field.

PhaseBreakdownPriorPhase.description: One entry in the `priorPhases` trigger-payload array — the steps-only output an earlier phase-breakdown turn emitted, paired with the journey step that earlier turn was expanding and its 2-D `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor. The journey-step is included so the current-phase prompt can render each prior phase under a human-readable label without re-deriving it from `journeySteps` on FlowContext (the trigger payload no longer carries `journeySteps`).

steps.description: Steps to materialize under their durable stages. Each step\'s `stageId` must resolve to an existing PlanStage on the plan.

PhaseBreakdownPlan.description: The structured plan the phase-breakdown agent emits for one journey step — a flat list of steps, each bound by `stageId` to the durable PlanStage the journey step belongs under. A phase emits steps only; it never authors stages, because the stage backbone is already durable from proposed-stages. Carried on the `DONE` completion\'s payload and accumulated on `PlanFromDesignDocFlowContext.accumulatedPhases` keyed by the `(stageIdx, phaseIdx)` cursor. The platform materializes every accumulated phase\'s steps in one transaction immediately before the FINALIZE transition fires; nothing is materialized during the agent loop.

id.description: Stable UUID handle for this step within the reviewed atomic change set.

dependsOnStepIds.description: Explicit prerequisite step handles, directed from this dependent step to each prerequisite. Omission or an empty array declares no prerequisites; sequenceOrder never implies a dependency. References must resolve within the complete retained plan. Full-set review must preserve intended prerequisites, redirect references from merged steps to retained handles, and remove references only when the prerequisite is no longer intended.

stageId.description: UUID of the durable PlanStage this step is materialized under — the same `stageId` carried on the trigger\'s `journeyStep`. The stage is authored by proposed-stages and already exists; this phase emits no stages of its own. Materialization fails if this id does not resolve to a stage on the plan.

title.description: Short product-language title for the step. Follows the same title conventions `create_step` / `create_steps` document.

description.description: Product-language description of the step\'s intent and scope. Acceptance criteria belong on `acceptanceCriteria`, not here.

implementation.description: Per-step prose description of the concrete change this step delivers, bound to a file from the paired PHASE_GROUNDING report\'s `touchPoints`. The submission tool cross-validates that this string references at least one repo-relative path the agent named in that report, so each step the platform materializes points back at the touch point that motivated it.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Required acceptance-criteria body for the step\'s backing entity. The value is one string containing newline-delimited markdown bullets (for example, `- First condition\\n- Second condition`), never a JSON array of strings. Every step must declare how its done-state will be verified; missing or empty is rejected at the submission boundary.

sequenceOrder.description: Zero-based ordering position of this step relative to its siblings under the same `stageId`.

serviceIds.description: Optional complete known set of platform Services that own or are modified by the work. Resolve every entry via `list_services` during the investigation pass. When supplied, materialization associates the backing task and PlanStep with every Service in the set. Omit only when Service scope is genuinely unresolved; never guess. Cross-Service work may remain one coherent step when its complete Service set is recorded.

designDocMotivation.description: A quoted excerpt or paraphrase of the design-doc passage that motivated this step — used to record a derived influence on the materialized proposal pointing back at the design doc. The agent must supply a non-empty value for every step; empty string is rejected at the submission boundary.

PhaseBreakdownStep.description: One step the phase-breakdown agent asks the platform to materialize under the durable PlanStage identified by `stageId`. `id` is a     stable UUID handle minted by the agent for the reviewed change set.     The platform materializes the step directly as a canonical STANDARD     Task; no PlanStep or duplicate backing entity is created.

PhaseBreakdownStepType.description: The step kind the phase-breakdown agent is asking the platform to materialize. Every step is a `TASK` — an implementation unit on the platform `PlanStepType` surface.

entityId.description: The Mockup or Diagram work item the approved proposal was enacted as.

summary.description: First paragraph of the work item\'s description; empty when the description is empty.

PlanShapingApprovedVisual.description: One Mockup or Diagram from the approved visual set, resolved server-side when the user approves the set. Approved visuals whose work item cannot be resolved are not listed.

designDocId.description: Canonical id of the plan\'s design document. Included in the batched get_full_entity call to ground the proposed stages in the approved design.

planId.description: Canonical id of the plan being shaped. Included in the batched get_full_entity call so the agent can read the plan and its existing stage/step proposals to author or revise stage proposals against the live plan state.

userMessage.description: Optional free-form text from the user (e.g. feedback on the proposed stages). Termination is enforced by the submit_ready submission tool, not by the payload.

PlanShapingProposedStagesPromptPayload.description: Payload for the plan-shaping proposed-stages EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=plan_shaping_proposed_stages). The agent produces the plan\'s stages at theme fidelity, each stage carrying its step themes, as platform proposals via the plan-shaping MCP tools. The wire payload carries the canonical handles for the design doc and the plan being shaped — the agent reads their current state in a single batched get_full_entity call (passing both ids as `{ entities: [{ entityType, entityId }, ...] }`) rather than relying on conversation history — plus the optional user message that triggered the turn.

planId.description: Canonical id of the plan whose stage is being refined. Included in the batched get_full_entity call to keep the expanded steps consistent with the surrounding stages.

stageId.description: Canonical id of the specific stage being refined. Included in the batched get_full_entity call so the agent can read the stage\'s existing theme rows and expand them into concrete step proposals.

userMessage.description: Optional free-form text from the user. Termination is enforced by the submit_ready submission tool, not by the payload.

PlanShapingRefineStagePromptPayload.description: Payload for the plan-shaping refine-stage EXTERNAL_AGENT node (promptType=plan_shaping_refine_stage). Fires when the user opens a stage in REFINING status from the plan UI; the agent reads the plan and stage in a single batched get_full_entity call (passing both ids as `{ entities: [{ entityType, entityId }, ...] }`) and expands the stage\'s theme rows into concrete step proposals via the plan-shaping MCP tools. The wire payload carries the canonical handles for the plan and the specific stage being refined, plus the validation toggle and the optional user message that triggered the turn.

PlanShapingValidationMode.description: Toggle controlling whether the agent runs the post-creation validation pass on its step proposals before submitting. `on` enables the validation pass (the agent re-reads its proposals and revises before terminating); `off` skips it so the agent submits its first-pass proposals directly. Used by the refine-stage node.

steps.description: The stage\'s drafted steps flattened from `accumulatedPhases[stageIdx]` in phaseIdx order. Every step carries its durable `stageId` and `sequenceOrder` from the phase-breakdown turn that produced it; the agent\'s tightened set must keep `stageId` unchanged and set `sequenceOrder` in intended final order (materialization sorts by it within a phase before re-numbering per stage).

stageIdx.description: Zero-based index of the stage under review within the plan\'s ordered durable stages. The agent MUST echo this value back verbatim on its `submit_step_review` payload so the API can detect cursor divergence and synthesize an ERROR-class completion.

The API uses `userMessage` to author the opening USER row, and the CLI uses the optional canonical `entity` to materialize a scoped Run. StartRunPromptPayload.description: Payload for the start-run envelope variant (AgentTriggerStartRun, sentinel promptType=`start_run`). Mirrors the fields of the Agent Bridge runtime contract in openapi/specs/agent-bridge/openapi.yaml that the CLI needs to materialize a Run on the host side. The platform start-run producer forwards this payload on the signed envelope so the CLI can materialize the Run without re-deriving any field. Carried inside an `AgentTriggerStartRun` whose discriminator value is the sentinel literal `start_run`. Two arms on the signed trigger envelope, distinguished by a `handlerPromptType` (turn-firing) vs `workflowName` (materialize-only) discriminator — exactly one discriminator is present on any given envelope: - **`handlerPromptType` + `payload` (turn-firing arm).** The   non-workflow case. The CLI materializes the Run and immediately   fires its first turn against `handlerPromptType`, driven by   `payload`. This is the only arm that drives turn one from the CLI. - **`workflowName` (materialize-only arm).** The workflow-orchestrated   case (e.g. plan mode). `handlerPromptType` is absent. A bind-only launch   omits `payload`; a kickoff launch carries a `workflow_kickoff` payload   with the opening user message and optional canonical focal `entity`.   The CLI materializes the Run and binds `conversationId → runId` but   fires no turn — the Temporal workflow (already started server-side)   drives every turn via its own signed SYSTEM triggers. Skipping   `start_run` entirely for a workflow session would leave no   `conversationId → runId` binding and the workflow\'s triggers would be   dropped as `no_active_run`; the materialize-only arm is how a launch   turn is suppressed without dropping the envelope.  On the kickoff form, the API authors the workflow arm\'s USER opening row from `payload.userMessage`, while the same payload supplies the CLI with the optional focal `entity` needed for Run materialization. Bind-only launches author no kickoff row and carry no payload. Independently of the arm discriminator, `triggersAgent` (default `true`) governs whether the turn-firing arm actually fires turn one. Setting it `false` turns a `handlerPromptType` + `payload` envelope materialize-only: the CLI materializes the Run and binds `conversationId → runId` but fires no turn. This is the non-workflow way to seed a standing greeting that waits for the user — the same launch-turn suppression the `workflowName` arm achieves by routing dispatch to a Temporal workflow.

launchStageId.description: Plan stage that contains `launchStepId`. targetSessionId.description: The platform `agentSession.id` (UUID) of the session this run is operating *against*, when the route observes another session rather than owning its own conversation alone. updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the task was last updated.

archivedAt.description: The timestamp when the task was archived (soft delete).

TaskResponseDto.description: A task within an organization. Polymorphic over TaskType; the same shape represents STANDARD, BUG, FEATURE, GOAL, DIAGRAM, DIAGRAM_ELEMENT, and TASK_MONITOR work items. GOAL tasks additionally carry `trackedEntities` — outgoing TRACKS-edge snapshots for the work the goal is tracking. Non-GOAL tasks omit the field or return an empty array. When requested, GOAL tasks also carry `trackedWorkSummary`, a compact count aggregate that is independent of the `trackedEntities` projection. FEATURE tasks carry `tag` (FeatureTag) classifying the feature; the field is absent on all non-FEATURE work-item types.

AgentEdgeType.description: Relationship type for agent-authored topology edges between two entities. Each value carries a distinct semantic: - RELATED_TO: source and target share context but have no directional   dependency, derivation, or replacement relationship. - DEPENDS_ON: source entity requires the target entity to be in place   (functionally or temporally) before it is meaningful or completable. - DERIVES_FROM: target entity is the origin or basis from which the   source entity was produced; the target remains canonical and the   source is a downstream artifact. - SUPERSEDES: source entity replaces the target entity; the target is   displaced and should no longer be treated as canonical. - CONTRADICTS: source entity disagrees with the target entity; both   remain visible so the conflict can be resolved by an authoring agent. - EVOLVES: source entity refines, extends, or iterates on the target   entity, which remains canonical. Distinct from SUPERSEDES (target is   displaced) and DERIVES_FROM (target is origin only and the source   stands apart). - TRACKS: source references the target as a tracked deliverable. The   meaning is composed with source and target type — the canonical   use is a GOAL-typed task referencing a FEATURE / STANDARD / BUG task   or a PLAN it expects to ship. DESIGN_DOC and other GOAL targets are   rejected at the attach boundary (track the parent feature or plan   instead). Validation lives in the boundary handler, not the edge   service. - PROPOSED_TOGETHER: source and target were created or modified by the   same proposal, making them co-authored siblings. Symmetric (the edge   carries no direction beyond the storage tuple) and system-emitted   (derived by the Graph service from a proposal-approved event rather   than authored by a user or agent). Carries no semantic claim about   dependency, derivation, or replacement — only that the two entities   share a proposal origin. Always paired with source `system`. - FULFILLED_BY: meta edge from a WORKFLOW_STEP work item to the work item   where that step\'s implementation lives. It remains visible in generic   meta-edge surfaces and is never categorized as flow. - STANDARD: flow edge from one WORKFLOW_STEP to the next ordinary step in   the same workflow graph. Carries category `flow`, requires direction,   and may carry an action label. - CONDITIONAL: flow edge from a WORKFLOW_STEP to the next branch selected   by a predicate. Carries category `flow` and requires both direction and   predicate. It may also carry an action label. - LOOP: flow edge representing a self-loop or return loop in a workflow   graph. Carries category `flow`, does not carry direction, and may carry   a predicate when the return is conditional. It may also carry an action   label.

AgentEdgeCategory.description: Rendering and traversal category for an edge. Existing edge records and callers that omit this field default to `meta`. Flow-category edges (`STANDARD`, `CONDITIONAL`, `LOOP`) are workflow structure and must stay out of generic related-entity, supersede/evolves, task-list, and link-discovery surfaces. Meta-category edges remain the regular topology and fulfillment surface.

AgentEdgeDirection.description: Direction declared on workflow flow edges where the direction matters to rendering or validation. `STANDARD` and `CONDITIONAL` edges require this field. `LOOP` edges do not carry it because the source step is also the return point.

WorkflowTransitionRole.description: Optional explicit meaning of a flow transition, independent of its action label, relationship variant, predicate and placement. `PRIMARY_PROGRESSION` is the main depicted journey, `ERROR_PATH` an unsuccessful or exceptional branch, `RECOVERY` a route back toward usable progress after something went wrong, and `RETURN` a move back to an earlier step without any failure, such as breadcrumb or back navigation. Absence means unclassified; the role is never inferred from labels, position or topology. Valid only on flow edges (`STANDARD`, `CONDITIONAL`, `LOOP`).

EdgeSource.description: Origin of an edge — who or what put it in the graph. Used by response surfaces that want to render or filter edges by provenance. - system: edge produced by platform code rather than authored by a   user or agent. Covers both structural edges created as part of an   entity\'s own lifecycle (e.g. HAS_TASK created when a task is   attached to a feature) and edges materialized by the Graph service   from a separate signal such as a proposal-approved event (e.g.   PROPOSED_TOGETHER edges). - agent: edge authored by an AI agent through the edge-proposal   surface, carrying agent reasoning. - user: edge authored directly by a human through the UI.

targetEntityTitle.description: Snapshot of the target entity\'s title at the moment the proposal was created. Optional on input — when omitted and `targetEntityType` is `TASK` or `DESIGN_DOC`, the server resolves the title from the EntityRegistry and stamps it before the row is persisted. For `PROPOSAL` targets with endpointMode PROPOSAL, the server snapshots the proposal title at authoring. ENTITY-mode proposal targets retain their deferred title semantics. ProposalEdgeDeclaration.description: endpointMode PROPOSAL requires targetEntityType PROPOSAL. It is only valid for PROPOSAL targets and deferred ENTITY mode. When omitted, the proposal root is the source.

ProposalEdgeEndpointMode.description: ENTITY (also the behavior when omitted) materializes entity relationships on approval, deferring proposal targets until approved. PROPOSAL stores a durable source-proposal to target-proposal relationship from authoring and requires targetEntityType PROPOSAL. Neither endpoint is replaced by its materialized entity. Pending, undecided, rejected, and approved targets retain the relationship. This is not an enactment prerequisite.

ProposalEdgeTargetType.description: Type of entity referenced by a declared proposal edge. `TASK` and `DESIGN_DOC` link to an already-materialized entity (the edge is created in the graph service immediately on approval). `PROPOSAL` references a proposal in the same organization and project. endpointMode determines whether proposal identities are retained or resolved on approval.

ProposalEdgeType.description: Relationship type for edges declared on proposals. Values are a proposal-scoped subset of the graph-service RelationshipType enum. `SUPERSEDES` is declared by the supersede transition: the proposal that sets a task\'s status to `SUPERSEDED` carries the matching `SUPERSEDES` edge to the successor task, so the status change and the edge travel on one reviewable proposal. `EVOLVES` marks that the source entity refines, extends, or iterates on the target entity, which remains canonical — distinct from `SUPERSEDES`, where the target is displaced. `TRACKS` is reserved for the server-authored declaration produced by a compound `CreateWorkItemTracksAttachment`; generic proposal edge inputs do not author it directly.

inputTokens.description: Fresh uncached input tokens; excludes cache reads.

EvalKnownCost.description: A cost read from the provider\'s own record. `partial` means only some of the attempt\'s provider sessions could be read, so the amount is a lower bound.

EvalUnavailableCost.description: The cost could not be read (unsupported provider such as OpenCode, no provider session, or a failed read). Carries no amount so it is never mistaken for zero.

omittedCalls.description: Number of further calls left out once the list reached its cap.

EvalRecordedToolCalls.description: The tool calls one attempt made, in order. UNAVAILABLE means they could not be collected, which is different from COLLECTED with no calls.

arguments.description: Serialized arguments the agent passed, cut to a fixed size when large.

origin.description: RUN_OBSERVED calls come from the Run\'s retained tool usage. INTERCEPTED is reserved for calls the CLI answered itself without performing them.

agentText.description: Text the agent wrote with an INTERCEPTED call.

FeatureSyncReportDiscrepancy.description: One row of the FEATURE_SYNC reconciliation table the agent rendered to the user. Each entry pairs the entity that looks off with a one-sentence product-language description of what was flagged.

FeatureSyncReportSourceType.description: Kind of entity a FEATURE_SYNC discrepancy row points at.

title.description: Human-readable title of the referenced entity (the `|title` half of the mention).

FeatureSyncReportSourceRef.description: Reference to the entity a FEATURE_SYNC discrepancy row points at. Mirrors the `Source` column of the user-facing reconciliation table — the agent renders this as `@[<entityType>:<entityId>|<title>]`.

FeatureSyncReportReconciliationOption.description: One numbered reconciliation option offered to the user under the discrepancy table. `description` is the product-language phrasing the agent showed; each `discrepancyIndex` is a 0-based index into the `discrepancies` array on this same payload, indicating which row(s) the option would resolve.

FeatureSyncDecisionGroup.description: One independent decision, not an entity-set bucket. Group ids are unique within the report; choice ids and typed targets are unique within a group. Independent groups may share targets. Producers validate these identities and exactly one no-change choice before persistence.

id.description: Stable identity unique within this group.

label.description: Concise choice label without ordinal prefixes.

isNoChange.description: Exactly one choice in each group must be true; validated before creation.

category.description: Free-form grouping label for the note. Suggested values include `hidden_requirements`, `constraints`, and `dependencies_discovered`, but the agent may use other categories when they fit better.

text.description: One discovery, written as a short prose note.

FeatureSyncHandoffReportNote.description: One categorized note the analyze agent recorded for the next phase. The note text is free prose; the category groups related notes (e.g. all constraints together) so a planner / implementer can scan by kind.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the decision lives in.

startLine.description: Post-edit start line (new-file side of the diff).

endLine.description: Post-edit end line (new-file side of the diff).

ImplementReportPayloadAllOfLocation.description: Anchor pointing at the specific code location that embodies this decision. Populate only for decisions realized in a concrete, nameable place in the code; omit it for decisions with no single location.

expectedOutcome.description: Short prose describing what the agent expects to happen at this file — the contract it expects to find, the change it intends to make, or the behavior it expects to confirm.

divergenceFromInitialPlan.description: When this touch point diverges from the prior approved plan, the short prose explanation of how and why. Omitted when the touch point matches the plan.

PhaseGroundingReportTouchPoint.description: One touch point an upcoming phase intends to land in: a specific file the agent will read or modify, paired with the outcome it expects there. `divergenceFromInitialPlan` is set only when this touch point differs from what the prior approved plan described — the absence of the field means the touch point matches the plan.

content.description: The proposed centerpiece, such as a DTO, table definition, or prose block.

connections.description: Optional evidence-bearing connections. Omit this property when no applicable connection is established.

sourceField.description: Field path or graph edge that establishes the connection.

sourceExcerpt.description: Complete source excerpt supporting the connection.

PlanReportPrimaryImplementationConnectio.description: Evidence-backed connection between a primary implementation and a resolved, non-archived workflow step or Contract. This records plan evidence only and does not create graph topology.

phase.description: 1-based phase this step belongs to. Steps sharing a phase number are grouped together in the execution sequence.

targetFiles.description: Repo-relative paths of files this step modifies. Omitted for purely investigative or read-only steps.

PlanReportSourceType.description: Kind of entity referenced from a PLAN report execution step or discrepancy.

ProjectReportPreset.description: Outline-guide provenance retaining the accepted question and edited outline. Applying a guide changes only the outline.

ProjectReportScope.description: Fixed UTC start-inclusive/end-exclusive window; start must precede end. timeZone is the display IANA timezone. Omitted actor/classification filters include all authorized matching evidence; empty classification arrays select none. Retains canonical queryActivity semantics.

ActivityCorrelationActivityType.description: Correlated activity category. - VIEWED: User focused or viewed an entity. - UNBLOCKED: Work progressed because a dependency or blocking condition was resolved. - NOTIFICATION: User-visible system or workflow notification tied to entity activity. - AGENT_SESSION_COMPLETED: A linked agent session reached COMPLETED status.

ActivityCorrelationSource.description: Source stream that produced the correlated activity item.

key.description: Opaque report-local evidence key. Authored body citations use data-evidence-key with this exact, case-sensitive value; the host resolves it through provenance.evidence, never as a URL or entity ID.

ProjectReportEvidenceReference.description: Host-owned evidence target. Current-state context is separate from selected-period evidence.

ProjectReportCoverage.description: COMPLETE accounts for all matching activity retrieved during generation. Bounds, failures or missing pages require INCOMPLETE and explicit limitations. Counts are live observations, not a snapshot guarantee.

ProjectReportBody.description: Static HTML/CSS in an isolated document. No scripts, external resources, executable navigation or escaping styles. Host owns evidence navigation and report presentation. Cite evidence using data-evidence-key attributes whose exact values match provenance.evidence keys. Repeated citations may reuse a key; producers should include one provenance entry per key. Unknown citations remain unresolved and inert.

ReviewReportDisposition.description: Optional durable outcome recorded by Review. CLEAN means the reviewed scope has no remaining findings. FIX_REQUIRED means Review could not safely finish or verify a required high-severity fix. USER_JUDGMENT means only non-blocking suggestions or explicit scope decisions remain for a person to evaluate.

command.description: Shell command to execute. Required when `type` is `command_line`.

workingDirectory.description: Optional repo-relative working directory the command should run from. Omitted means the service root.

ValidationAction.description: One executable action inside a VALIDATION_WALKTHROUGH step. Discriminated union on `type`.
